card.tip: 不 is bù, but it becomes bú when the next syllable is 4th tone (是 shì, 要 yào, 客 kè, 姓 xìng, 叫 jiào, 看 kàn).

points.en: What do you like to eat and drink?

examples: nǐ xǐ huān hē shén me?
What do you like to drink?
wǒ xǐ huān hē zhēn zhū nǎi chá.
wǒ bù xǐ huān chī hàn bǎo.
card.tip: 喝 is for drinks, 吃 for food. The answer keeps the question's word order: just put the thing where 什麼 was.

items.ctx: Q：你喜歡喝什麼？

items.en: What do you not like to eat?

examples: What would you like to drink?
wǒ bú yào hē kě lè.
card.tip: 要 = to want, right now (ordering, choosing). 喜歡 = to like, in general. Before 要, 不 is said bú: 不要 bú yào.

items.ctx: A：你要喝什麼？
A：你要喝咖啡嗎？
items.en: No, I don't want coffee, I want tea.

items.ctx: A：你要吃漢堡嗎？
items.q: B：我不要吃漢堡，我＿吃沙拉。
items.en: I don't want a hamburger, I want a salad.
What would you like to eat?
What would you like to drink?
I want to eat soup dumplings.

examples: nǐ jué de shén me hěn hǎo hē?
What do you think tastes good?
wǒ jué de wū lóng chá hěn hǎo hē.
I think oolong tea tastes good.
wǒ jué de pí jiǔ bù hǎo hē.
I don't think beer tastes good.
card.tip: After 覺得 comes a whole little sentence: the thing + 很 / 不 + 好喝 (drinks), 好看 (looks), 好玩 (fun).

items.en: I think red wine tastes good.
I don't think tennis is fun.
I think this photo is pretty.

items.ctx: Q：你覺得什麼很好喝？
opts: 我覺得珍珠奶茶很好喝。
我覺得很好喝珍珠奶茶。
珍珠奶茶覺得我很好喝。
items.en: I think bubble tea tastes good.
I don't think cola tastes good.

examples: lǎo shī yǒu jǐ zhāng zhào piàn?
How many photos does the teacher have?
lǎo shī yǒu sān zhāng zhào piàn.
nǐ yǒu jǐ ge gē ge?
How many older brothers do you have?
card.tip: 幾 asks "how many" when you expect a small number. Keep the measure word: 幾張照片, 幾個人, 幾本書. In the answer, put the number where 幾 was; 2 is 兩, not 二.

items.ctx: A：老師有幾張照片？
A：你有幾個姐姐？

items.en: How many books do you have?
How many people are in his family?
How many photos do you have?

patterns: {s:Pronoun} + ({k:的}) + {o:family, 家, 學校, 班, 公司}
examples: zhāng xiān shēng de tài tai
card.tip: 的 means "'s / of". After a pronoun (我, 你們, 他們…) you can drop it before family and before groups you belong to (家, 學校, 班, 公司). Keep it before things (書, 房子, 車) and after names (張先生的…).

examples: wǒ men jīn tiān wǎn shàng yào qù kàn diàn yǐng.
We're going to see a movie tonight.
tā xīng qí yī zǎo shàng zuò shén me?
What does he do on Monday mornings?
tā xīng qí yī zǎo shàng xué zhōng wén.
He studies Chinese on Monday mornings.
card.tip: The time word (今天晚上, 明天早上, 星期一, 週末) goes right after the subject, before the verb. Putting it first (今天晚上我們…) is also heard, but the handout teaches S + TW + VO.

items.en: We're going to see a movie tonight.
He often plays basketball on weekends.
What are you doing this evening?
Tomorrow evening we'll eat Vietnamese food together.
He takes photos on Tuesday evenings.
He plays baseball on Tuesday mornings.
He makes dinner on Wednesday evenings.
He plays tennis on Monday evenings.

examples: tā yě shì rì běn rén.
wǒ men dōu hěn xǐ huān dǎ lán qiú.
We all like playing basketball a lot.
wǒ cháng qù kàn diàn yǐng.
I often go to the movies.
wǒ bù cháng dǎ wǎng qiú.
card.tip: All three go after the subject and before the verb. 也 = also, too. 都 = all, both (the subject is plural: 我們, 他們, A和B). 常 = often; not often is 不常. Together: 也都, 都常.

items.ctx: A：你是日本人，他呢？
A：你們喜歡打籃球嗎？
items.en: We all like playing basketball a lot.

items.ctx: A：週末你常做什麼？
items.en: I often go to the movies.

items.ctx: A：我想吃臺灣菜。
items.en: OK! I want Taiwanese food too.

items.ctx: A：我常和朋友一起打網球，你呢？
items.q: B：我＿打網球。我覺得打網球不好玩。
items.en: I don't often play tennis. I don't think tennis is fun.

items.ctx: A：你爸爸媽媽是美國人嗎？
A：我喜歡游泳。
A：我喜歡吃臺灣菜和越南菜。
items.q: B：臺灣菜、越南菜，我＿喜歡吃。
items.en: Taiwanese and Vietnamese food, I like both too.
We both often eat Vietnamese food.
I also like listening to music.

points.zh: A 和 B · 也 · 都

examples: wǒ xǐ huān tīng yīn yuè hàn dǎ lán qiú.
I like listening to music and playing basketball.
{s:我}{v:喜歡}{o:聽音樂}，{k:也}{v:喜歡}{o:打籃球}。
wǒ xǐ huān tīng yīn yuè, yě xǐ huān dǎ lán qiú.
I like listening to music, and I also like playing basketball.
tīng yīn yuè hàn dǎ lán qiú, wǒ dōu xǐ huān.
Music and basketball, I like both.
card.tip: 和 only joins two things (nouns or activities), never two sentences: for that use 也. With 都, the two things come first, because 都 points back to them.

items.ctx: Say it with 也: 我喜歡看書和看電影。
Say it with 都: 我喜歡游泳和踢足球。
你想吃越南菜還是美國菜？ (You want both.)
你想看美國電影還是臺灣電影？ (You want both.)

items.q: 我喜歡喝茶，＿喜歡喝咖啡。
items.en: I like tea, and I also like coffee.
Tea and coffee, I like both.

opts: 我喜歡打網球，也喜歡打棒球。
我喜歡打網球，和喜歡打棒球。
我也喜歡打網球，喜歡打棒球。
items.en: I like tennis, and I also like baseball.

opts: 網球和棒球，我都喜歡打。
網球和棒球，都我喜歡打。
我網球和棒球，喜歡都打。
items.en: Tennis and baseball, I like playing both.

examples: nǐ xǐ huān hē chá hái shì hē kā fēi?
Do you like tea or coffee?
nǐ xiǎng chī yuè nán cài hái shì měi guó cài?
Do you want Vietnamese or American food?
yuè nán cài hàn měi guó cài, wǒ dōu xiǎng chī.
Vietnamese and American food, I want both.
card.tip: 還是 already makes it a question, so there's no 嗎 at the end. Answer with one of the two, or with 都 (both) or 都不 (neither).

items.q: 陳小姐喜歡喝啤酒還是喝咖啡？
opts: 喝啤酒和喝咖啡，她都喜歡。

items.q: 王小姐喜歡看書還是看電影？
opts: 看書和看電影，她都喜歡。
items.en: Reading and movies, she likes both.

items.q: 李先生喜歡踢足球還是打籃球？
opts: 踢足球和打籃球，他都不喜歡。
踢足球和打籃球，他都喜歡。
items.en: Football and basketball, he likes neither.

opts: 他喜歡喝茶還是喝咖啡？
他喜歡喝茶還是喝咖啡嗎？
他喜歡喝茶和咖啡還是？
items.en: Does he like tea or coffee?

items.ctx: A：你是美國人還是日本人？

items.en: Do you want to eat Taiwanese or Vietnamese food?
Do you like swimming or playing tennis?

examples: nǐ cháng chī tái wān cài ma?
Do you often eat Taiwanese food?
wǒ bù cháng chī tái wān cài.
I don't often eat Taiwanese food.
tái wān cài, wǒ bù cháng chī.
Taiwanese food, I don't often eat it.
card.tip: Put the thing you're talking about first, add a comma, then say the rest of the sentence without it. Very common when answering a question about that thing.

items.ctx: Topic first: 我不常吃臺灣菜。

你常看書嗎？ Answer topic first.
Q：你想學中文嗎？

items.en: Chinese, I want to learn it.
Football, I don't often play it.

items.ctx: Q：你喜歡越南菜嗎？
items.en: Vietnamese food, I like it a lot.

examples: zhōu mò wǒ men qù yóu yǒng, hǎo bù hǎo?
Shall we go swimming this weekend?
我不喜歡游泳，{s:我們}{v:去打網球}{k:吧}！
wǒ bù xǐ huān yóu yǒng, wǒ men qù dǎ wǎng qiú ba!
I don't like swimming, let's go play tennis!
card.tip: 吧 at the end turns a sentence into a suggestion: "let's…". To ask what the other person thinks, end with 好不好？ or 怎麼樣？ Answer 好啊！ or 不好。

items.ctx: A：週末我們去游泳，好不好？
items.q: B：我不喜歡游泳，我們去打網球＿！

items.en: Let's go eat Taiwanese food together tomorrow evening!
This weekend let's go to the movies, how about it?

examples: yì qiān sān bǎi duō kuài qián
a cup and a bit of coffee
card.tip: 多 goes right after the last round number you say: 1378 → 一千多 (1001–1999), 一千三百多 (1301–1399), 一千三百七十多 (1371–1379). For less than one extra unit (2.5 buns), 多 goes after the measure word: 兩個多包子.

items.ctx: A：你有幾杯咖啡？(1–2 杯)
items.en: I have a cup and a bit of coffee.

examples: yì bēi kā fēi duō shǎo qián?
How much is a cup of coffee?
yì bēi kā fēi wǔ shí wǔ kuài qián.
A cup of coffee is 55 dollars.
liǎng běn shū yì qiān bā bǎi kuài qián.
card.tip: 多少 asks how much or how many for any amount (幾 is for small numbers). 塊 is the measure word for dollars. Measure words: 杯 cups, 張 flat things (照片), 本 books, 支 phones, 瓶 bottles, 個 most other things. You can also say 一杯咖啡要多少錢？

items.en: A cup of coffee is 55 dollars.

opts: 一支手機兩萬三千八百塊錢。
一支手機二十三千八百塊錢。
一本手機兩萬三千八百塊錢。

items.en: A bottle of cola is 35 dollars.
How much is a bottle of beer?
How much is a cup of coffee?

points.zh: 買 · 賣 · 幫 · 一共

examples: qǐng wèn nín yào mǎi shén me?
What would you like to buy?
yì bēi kā fēi mài duō shǎo qián?
How much is a cup of coffee?
bāo zi, qǐng bāng wǒ wéi bō.
Please microwave the bun for me.
yí gòng bā shí wǔ kuài qián.
card.tip: 買 mǎi (3rd tone) = to buy, 賣 mài (4th tone) = to sell: the customer 買, the shop 賣. 幫 + person + verb = do something for someone. 一共 = altogether.

items.en: What would you like to buy?

items.q: 老闆：一杯咖啡＿八十塊錢。
items.en: A cup of coffee sells for 80 dollars.
I'd like to buy two books.
Please microwave the bun for me.

items.ctx: 客人：一個包子和一杯咖啡多少錢？
客人：請幫我微波。

items.en: I'd like to buy a bottle of cola.

points.zh: 大 / 中 / 小 · 外帶 / 內用
points.en: Ordering: size, take away or eat in

examples: 咖啡，{s:你}要{o:大杯}、{o:中杯}{k:還是}{o:小杯}？
kā fēi, nǐ yào dà bēi, zhōng bēi hái shì xiǎo bēi?
nǐ yào wài dài hái shì nèi yòng?
nǐ xǐ huān dà chē hái shì xiǎo chē?
Do you like big cars or small cars?
card.tip: 大 / 中 / 小 go before the measure word or noun: 大杯, 小車. With three choices, put 、 between the first two and 還是 before the last. 外帶 = take away, 內用 = eat in.

items.ctx: A：咖啡，你要大杯、中杯還是小杯？
A：一個人去吃飯，你常外帶還是內用？

opts: 你要大杯、中杯還是小杯？
你要大杯、中杯還是小杯嗎？
你要大杯還是、中杯小杯？

items.en: Do you want to take away or eat in?
I'd like a large bubble tea.
Do you like big cars or small cars?
Do you (plural) like to take away or eat in?

points.en: Can: three ways to say two things

examples: zhè zhī shǒu jī néng shàng wǎng hàn zhào xiàng.
This phone can go online and take photos.
zhè zhī shǒu jī néng shàng wǎng, yě néng zhào xiàng.
This phone can go online, and it can also take photos.
shàng wǎng hàn zhào xiàng, zhè zhī shǒu jī dōu néng.
Going online and taking photos, this phone can do both.
card.tip: 能 = can, to be able to. It works like 喜歡 A 和 B: 也 and 都 go before 能 (也能, 都能).

items.q: 這支手機能上網，＿能照相。
items.en: This phone can go online, and it can also take photos.

items.q: 上網和照相，這支手機＿能。
items.en: Going online and taking photos, this phone can do both.
This phone can go online and take photos.

opts: 這支手機能上網，也能照相。
這支手機能上網，能也照相。
這支手機也上網，能照相。
items.en: This phone can go online, and it can also take photos.

items.ctx: Say it with 也: 我的手機能上網和照相。
Say it with 都: 這支手機能上網和照相。
